lastCompletedStory.title: WARNING: US-002's change to release.yml ships with zero committed guard. US-001…

nextStoryContext:
Closed the reviewer-filed WARNING (.github/workflows/release.yml:33): release.yml's `gh release create` invocation and its attest step/permissions had zero committed guard, even though check-ci-parity.ts only ever reads ci.yml by design (patterns.md:1190) and the workflow only runs on a version-tag push (no PR-time CI catches a regression). Added test/release-workflow.test.ts, a static-source guard mirroring test/build-release-smoke.test.ts and test/ci-workflow.test.ts: reads the real .github/workflows/release.yml and pins (a) dist/SHA256SUMS.txt as an argument of the SAME gh release create invocation as the four binaries (scoped by slicing from 'gh release create' to the next '      - name:' step boundary, not a whole-file substring match, so a regression that moves SHA256SUMS.txt to an unrelated step would still fail), and (b) the actions/attest-build-provenance@v4 step plus the permissions block carrying id-token: write, attestations: write, and contents: write (also block-scoped, sliced between 'permissions:' and the next '\njobs:' line). Verified both legs are falsifiable before trusting them: manually deleted the SHA256SUMS.txt line from release.yml -> test failed with the expected diagnostic; manually deleted the attestations: write permission -> test failed with the expected diagnostic; restored the file byte-identical via diff both times (not just re-running unchanged). Step 5.5: WebFetch against docs.github.com/actions/security-guides/using-artifact-attestations-to-establish-provenance-for-builds confirmed actions/attest-build-provenance requires id-token: write and attestations: write (contents: read for attest alone; this job additionally needs contents: write for gh release create itself, which the workflow already has) -- matches the test's assertions exactly, no correction needed. Full spine clean: typecheck 0 errors, bun test 6007 pass / 0 fail across 359 files, bun run check:all all sub-gates ok (test, embed-vendor, lint, file-size, debt-markers, version-skips, coverage, dead-code, dup, ci-parity, agents-md, test-sleeps, skip-ratchet). No file-size/coverage budget raises needed (new file, no existing file grew). Only new file: test/release-workflow.test.ts.

Per prd.json, both US-R1-001 and US-R1-002 were the two reviewer-filed WARNING follow-ups (priority 1-2, requires:none) from the review round recorded in prd.json's review block (roundsCompleted:1, lastVerdict:'FIXES_PENDING:2'); the five original US-00X stories were renumbered priority 3-7 and remain the next likely dispatch targets after this one, still passes:false as of this write (I do not edit prd.json's passes field myself).
